summary: AE + SE intro; customer context: Pelican is building personalized summarization and realtime alerts for enterprise customers, currently using a mix of OpenAI hosted and an in-house model for POCs. Main concerns: predictable unit cost, latency SLOs for 300ms p50 alerts, and data residency/SOC2 needs. Explored Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs. Discussed batching, prefix caching/KV cache, quantization implications, and potential rollout approach. Concrete next steps: share pricing scenarios, bench run, and sample prompts.
topics: hosted vs dedicated vs private tradeoffs
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-15 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~55 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Ethan Liu (Redwood SE), Jordan Reyes (CTO - Pelican), Anika Shah (Lead ML Eng), Carlos Mendez (SRE), Priya Nair (Product)

---
00:00 Maya Patel: Hi everyone, thanks for taking time. Maya from Redwood, I'm the AE on this. Quick round robin?
00:09 Jordan Reyes: Hey Maya, Jordan here, CTO. We're trying to get a handle on inference unit costs vs latency for our summarization pipeline.
00:16 Anika Shah: Anika, lead ML, we'll probably be the people digging into the prompts and the evals.
:20 Carlos Mendez: Carlos, SRE, I'll care about p95/p99 and whether we can keep things in a VPC.
00:26 Maya Patel: Nice, thanks. Ethan, do you want to intro from SE side?
00:29 Ethan Liu: Sure, Ethan Liu. I'll focus on the performance, KV/prefix caching, and how batching configs change per-token cost and tail latency. We're going to go through three scenarios: hosted quick start, dedicated reserved capacity, and private deployment with VPC.
00:43 Jordan Reyes: Sounds good. We're mostly leaning to start hosted but need to understand how that scales into dedicated and whether we can keep costs predictable. Our CFO wants a 6-month runway and a hard cap on monthly inference spend.
00:55 Maya Patel: Totally. Quick question: what's your current throughput and average token length?
01:01 Anika Shah: Right now it's small — like 70 reqs/min average for the POC but peaks to 500 reqs/min when alerts run. Prompt+response average is about 450 tokens, but summarization responses can be 1k tokens sometimes.
01:14 Ethan Liu: Ok, so you have both mid and long sequence behavior. That affects batching heuristics and kernel selection. If you use longer sequences the per-token cost increases non-linearly unless you leverage KV cache or prefix caching.
01:30 Jordan Reyes: Can you quantify that? Like, how much do we save with KV cache?
01:34 Ethan Liu: Rough ballpark — for cases where a lot of the prompt is shared across requests, KV/prefix caching can cut GPU time by 30-60% for subsequent tokens. If you also enable dynamic batching, you might see another 15-30% improvement, but there's a latency tradeoff.
01:51 Carlos Mendez: Latency is a hard SLO for us. We want p50 ~300ms for alerts and p95 under 800ms ideally.
01:59 Maya Patel: That's useful. Hosted Redwood API has options for low-latency endpoints and we can configure lower-latency routing; however, the unit price for hosted includes multiple operational costs. Dedicated will give you more predictable per-token above a committed baseline. Private gives full control but has higher fixed costs.
02:17 Anika Shah: Can you show an example pricing scenario comparing hosted per-token vs dedicated reserved?
02:22 Maya Patel: We'll send a spreadsheet, but quick example: hosted text-generation might be X cents per 1k input tokens and Y cents per 1k output tokens on average. Dedicated with a monthly reserved pool amortized across tokens can drop per-token cost by 30-50% at steady high utilization, but if utilization is low the amortized cost looks worse.
02:40 Ethan Liu: Also, quantization can change compute by 2-4x depending on model and hardware. Lower precision helps cost but we need to validate quality for summarization; often 4-bit/8-bit quantization with calibration preserves quality.
02:56 Jordan Reyes: Ok so we need a matrix: traffic, model size, quantization, caching, and result cost.
03:03 Maya Patel: Exactly. We'll model three scenarios: small (hosted bursty), medium (dedicated committed for steady baseline with hosted overflow), and private (on-prem or VPC for residency). We'll include a sensitivity analysis on batch size and cache hit rates.
03:18 Anika Shah: For batching, what's the typical impact on tail latency? If we batch to improve throughput, does p95 blow up?
03:23 Ethan Liu: There's a balance. Continuous batching with a small max latency window (e.g., 10-20ms) can increase p95 slightly but often stays within SLOs. The bigger risk is waiting to accumulate large batches — that can push p95 beyond your target. We recommend adaptive batching with service-level sliders: target p50, p95 caps.
03:41 Carlos Mendez: How does fallback work if a dedicated pool is saturated? Do requests fail or get routed to hosted?
03:47 Maya Patel: You can set automatic fallback policies — e.g., overflow to hosted, or fallback to a cheaper model variant with lower quality but faster/cheaper execution. That keeps availability while bounding cost.
03:58 Jordan Reyes: About private deployments — we have regulatory customers in EU who demand EU-only processing. Is Redwood Private able to be deployed in EU-only with KMS?
04:06 Ethan Liu: Yes, Private supports customer-managed cloud in EU regions and integrates with KMS/HSM for key controls. We can also run audit logs and integrate SSO/SAML and RBAC for teams. We'll mark this as a hard constraint if you need EU residency.
04:19 Priya Nair: SOC2 is also required; do you have SOC2 and can we get the report?
04:23 Maya Patel: Redwood is SOC2 compliant; we'll share the compliance pack and the SOC2 attestation during follow-up.
04:29 Anika Shah: Back to unit econ — what are the levers we can tune quickly? Batching window, KV cache TTL, model quantization, routing to cheaper variants?
04:36 Ethan Liu: Yep. TTL/config for cache, prefix deduping, request shaping (e.g., truncate non-essential history), and adaptive quantization per-route are key levers. Also reranking or hallucination-detection can reduce output tokens by avoiding verbose replies.
04:50 Jordan Reyes: Do you have examples of customers who moved from hosted to dedicated and their observed savings?
04:55 Maya Patel: We can share anonymized case studies. Typical mid-size customers see 25-45% reduction in token cost after moving to dedicated and optimizing batching and cache. The exact number depends on traffic shape.
05:06 Anika Shah: For the bench run, what do you need from us?
05:09 Ethan Liu: Two things: a representative prompt set (50-200 prompts across short/medium/long) and a 2-week traffic CSV showing request times and sizes. We'll simulate caching and batching to estimate token cost and latency.
05:20 Maya Patel: Also let us know target monthly budget cap so we can build a scenario that meets it.
05:24 Jordan Reyes: CFO gave a soft cap of $25k/month for inference initially. If we can keep below that with dedicated or hybrid approach, it'll be a win.
05:32 Maya Patel: Ok we'll include a path that targets $25k with expected quality.
05:35 Carlos Mendez: A quick question — do you support customer-side quantization workflows or are you doing it in your runtime?
05:40 Ethan Liu: We support optimized quantized model variants in the runtime; customers can bring quantized models but we also have tooling to quantize during onboarding and validate quality. For private deployments you can bring your own artifacts with a validation pass.
05:51 Anika Shah: Any gotchas with 8k tokens? We sometimes hit 8k in long summaries.
05:56 Ethan Liu: Models with 8k context change memory/KV patterns. Batching is trickier because big contexts consume GPU memory; effective batching may be lower. We often recommend using prefix caching aggressively for shared context across requests and use streaming for long outputs so latency looks better for p50 even if total generation time is significant.
06:17 Jordan Reyes: Could you sketch an initial rollout plan?
06:20 Maya Patel: Sure — Phase 1: Hosted pilot with low-latency endpoint and KV cache turned on, measure cache hit and per-token costs. Phase 2: If utilization justifies, move to Dedicated reserved pool for baseline with hosted overflow. Phase 3 (optional): Private/VPC for customers requiring EU residency or extra controls. We'll include canary and A/B rollouts in all phases.
06:41 Priya Nair: Will we get observability at token-level and per-route cost in the console?
06:45 Ethan Liu: Yes — Redwood Console exposes token-level cost breakdown, latency distributions, and per-route tracing. You can set alerts if unit costs or latencies drift.
06:54 Jordan Reyes: Any quick numbers on how much prefix caching helps on our averaging? If our prompts share templates 80% of the time, what hit rate do you see?
06:59 Ethan Liu: If prompts are templated and only a few fields change, we often see cache hit rates above 60-80% on subsequent requests. First request always primes the cache. That means marginal cost for repeats is much lower.
07:14 Anika Shah: Are there any constraints for token accounting when using caching? Like do you still bill for all tokens?
07:20 Maya Patel: Billing typically accounts for actual compute performed. If caching avoids recomputing certain tokens, those cost savings show up in the unit econ. We'll clarify the exact billing lines in the pricing doc.
07:31 Jordan Reyes: Ok. Any concerns about model fidelity when using 4-bit quant? Our summaries need to retain nuance.
07:36 Ethan Liu: We'll validate. In many cases 4-bit quant with per-channel scaling preserves quality enough for summarization, but we should A/B test on your dev prompts. We'll include a quality regression threshold in the eval plan.
07:50 Carlos Mendez: From SRE side, for the bench run can we see what manifests for p95 on our traffic? We want to know whether p95 spikes at peak.
07:57 Ethan Liu: Yes, we'll run the bench with your peak traffic and show p50/p95/p99. We'll test both dedicated pool and hosted fallback.
08:05 Maya Patel: Quick recap: Redwood will send pricing scenarios + unit econ spreadsheet, SE will run bench sim once prompt set and traffic CSV are shared, customer will confirm residency and SOC2 docs.
08:17 Jordan Reyes: Great. Any blockers we haven't covered?
08:20 Priya Nair: Just timing — we want bench results within a week so leadership can decide.
08:25 Maya Patel: We'll aim for bench by 2026-04-20.
08:27 Anika Shah: One small nit: can you include suggestions for prompt truncation rules — like how to cut context without losing performance?
08:33 Ethan Liu: Yep, we'll include heuristics: drop low-signal tokens, compress history, and use retrieval-augmented contexts where possible.
08:41 Jordan Reyes: Thanks all.
08:43 Maya Patel: Thank you. We'll follow up with the deck and the spreadsheet.
09:00 [call ends]
